case_name: Ramappa Halappa Pujar And Others` v State Of Karnataka
respondent:
State Of Karnataka`
Supreme Court of India

27 April 2007
Appeal (Crl.) 1344 of 2005
The Judgment was delivered by: S. B. Sinha, J.
1. Appellants herein have filed this statutory appeal under the Supreme Court (Enlargement of Criminal Appellate Jurisdiction) Act, 1970 being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment dated 9.6.2005 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court of Karnataka at Bangalore in Criminal Appeal No.252 of 1999(A) whereby and whereunder, a judgment of acquittal passed by a III Additional Sessions Judge, Dharwad acquitting the appellants herein for offence punishable under sections 143, 147, 148, 341, 324, 342, 504 and 302 read with S. 149 of I.P.C. was reversed.
2. The alleged occurrence took place at about 10.30 A.M. on 13.12.1994 near the Bus stand at Village Ichangi situated in the District of Dharwad. A First Information Report was lodged by one Devendrappa (PW-25). He is the brother of appellants 1 and 2 herein being
facts: The alleged occurrence took place at about 10:30 A.M. on 13.12.1994 near the Bus stand at Village Ichangi situated in the District of Dharwad.
A First Information Report was lodged by one Devendrappa (PW-25).
Appellants 1 and 2 and the first informant allegedly sold 5 acres 20 gunthas of land situated in the said Village Ichangi to deceased Ratnavva.
The property, however was in possession of the deceased Ratnavva.
On 13.12.1994 at about 7:30 A.M. Ratnavva and her sons Shivananda Basavaraj and Veeresh went to the land in question for plucking groundnuts.
issues: Whether the High Court erred in reversing the judgment of acquittal recorded by the learned Trial Judge?
Whether the evidence of PWs.26 to 28 can be relied upon despite being close relatives of the deceased?
petitioner_arguments: Sufficient and cogent reasons having been assigned in support of the judgment of acquittal recorded by the learned Trial Judge which was based on probability and the view taken by it being a possible one, the High Court committed a manifest error in reversing the said judgment of acquittal.
respondent_arguments: The evidence of PWs.26 to 28 does not suffer from any infirmity and their testimony given in Court stands corroborated from the medical evidence on record.
court_reasoning: The Division Bench of the High Court opining that there was no reason to disbelieve the said PWs.25 to 28, particularly when PW.25 was an injured witness, differed with the said findings holding: ...

Therefore the mere fact that PWs.26 to 28 are the close relatives of the deceased is not sufficient to discard their testimony given in Court, more so, when their evidence does not suffer from any such infirmity.
holding: The appellants were convicted by the High Court under sections 143, 147, 148, 341, 342, and 302 read with S.149 of I.P.C.
They were sentenced to undergo imprisonment for life and a fine of Rs.1,000/for commission of the offence u/s.302 read with S.149 of the IPC.
